I've attached the RFP excerpt (Regulus_RFP_Section4.pdf).

Specifically we need:
- A description of your operator onboarding and offboarding process for private installs (incl. role definitions and minimum background checks).
- How you handle hardware-bound keying (HSM/KMS) during an air-gapped install.
- Certification steps you provide — for example, operator-run checklist items and sign-off artifacts.
- Evidence of training plan and a sample runbook for routine patching and rollback.

Can you please provide a single consolidated response we can share with our compliance reviewers? We also expect a lightweight PoC for one hospital to demonstrate the install and operator handoff.

Hi Laura, Jordan, Irene —

Below is a concise but operationally actionable response to the items in Section 4. I'll follow up with the full runbook PDF and training outline (attached). If Regulus wants a version with hospital-specific wording, we can adapt before final delivery.

1) Operator onboarding / offboarding (summary)
- Roles: Operator (day-to-day host/app ops), Installer (initial bootstrap and HW handling), auditor (read-only access for compliance).
- Minimum checks: vendor identity verification + two professional references (standard). For hospital environments where Regulus requires stricter vetting, we will accept hospital-provided badge provisioning and an on-site escort policy.
- Access model: Operators are assigned scoped RBAC roles with time-limited activation. All operator sessions require MFA (hardware token OR mobile app) and ephemeral credentials via short-lived certificates issued by the local PKI.

2) HSM / KMS handling in air-gapped installs
- Support matrix:
  * Fully air-gapped: Customer-provided FIPS 140-2/3 certified HSM generates root keys on-site. Redwood provides sealed software bundles and signed artifacts; we do NOT transmit root key material off-network.
  * Hybrid: Customer HSM generates and retains master keys; Redwood packages an encrypted key-wrapping bundle that is imported on-prem with verification using HSM-attested public keys.
- Key zeroization: documented procedure in runbook; remote command support only if customer authorizes out-of-band signed attestation.

3) Install certification pathway (what we deliver)
- Stage 1: Pre-install validation (network isolation checklist, HW inventory, signed manifest).
- Stage 2: Installer-led bootstrap (HSM init, operator role creation, audit config). Installer provides a bootstrap artifact and a signed install log.
- Stage 3: Operator acceptance testing (OAT) — operators execute a factory OAT script; results are collected as a signed JSON manifest and archived.
- Stage 4: Certification sign-off — operator + customer security engineer sign an install certificate (PDF) confirming checks complete.

4) Training and runbook
- Training: 2-day operator course (onsite or remote proctored) + annually required refresh. Certification issued on completion with unique cert ID.
- Runbook: we provide a sample runbook covering routine patching, emergency rollback, operator escalation flow, and HSM handling. Sample attached (Regulus_Runbook_Sample.pdf) and training outline (operator-training-outline.pdf).

Notes/constraints:
- We maintain a small set of privileged deployers who can create sealed bundles; those employees are subject to background checks and additional attestation for air-gapped projects.
- We do not retain customer proprietary keys for air-gapped installs.

Attachments: operator-training-outline.pdf

Happy to schedule a 60-minute walk-through with your security & ops teams next week.

Regards,

Laura / Tom —

Thanks for the quick review. Per Vanessa's draft above, attached are the requested artifacts: a redacted sample install log and a redacted OAT manifest (both included inside Regulus_Runbook_Sample.pdf), plus the training outline and preflight checklist we discussed. Key clarifications: 

- Signed artifacts: we use an RSA-3072 signature over a canonical JSON manifest with the following fields: install_id, installer_id, host_fingerprint, hsm_attestation, timestamp, signer_cert_sn. Redacted examples included.
- Privileged deployer notice: standard is 5 business days for background verification and provisioning. For hospitals requiring advanced vetting, we typically align to the hospital's vendor onboarding window (7–15 business days) and can supply attestation docs on request.
- Training: includes a mandatory 2hr hands-on lab during the course where each operator completes a bootstrap + rollback scenario and receives a pass/fail practical assessment. Successful completion yields a downloadable cert with a unique cert ID.

Proposed next steps: 
1) We will post a polished answer packet to the shared drive by EOD (https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Regulus-RFP-answers).
2) Schedule a 60-minute technical review Wednesday 2028-07-03 at 10:00 AM ET — tentative link: https://calendly.com/redwood/jb-onprem-demo-60m.
3) For the PoC: propose a 3-week timeline from kickoff (week 0 prep, week 1 install, week 2 OAT & acceptance).

If you want additional paperwork (insurance riders, on-site SOW language), we can pull examples into the packet prior to the technical review.
